ComponentTypes.name: LLM Application
ComponentTypes.description: An application integrating a Large Language Model that processes user inputs and system prompts together without clear separation.

ComponentTypes.name: LLM Agent
ComponentTypes.description: An advanced LLM system with reasoning capabilities, working memory, and access to external tools or APIs.

ComponentTypes.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) System
ComponentTypes.description: A system that fetches contextual information from external knowledge bases or vector databases to augment LLM queries.

ComponentTypes.name: Vector Database
ComponentTypes.description: A database used to store document embeddings for RAG systems, which can be vulnerable to data poisoning.

ComponentTypes.name: Multimodal LLM
ComponentTypes.description: A Large Language Model capable of processing non-textual inputs like images, audio, or document structures alongside text.

ComponentTypes.name: Guardrail Model
ComponentTypes.description: An independent model (LLM-as-judge) used to filter inputs, screen outputs, or evaluate proposed actions of the primary LLM.

Capabilities.name: Process Natural Language
Capabilities.description: The foundational ability to parse and process natural language instructions and data streams simultaneously.

Capabilities.name: Access External Tools
Capabilities.description: The ability of an LLM agent to dynamically invoke external functions, APIs, or operational tools based on its reasoning.

Capabilities.name: Retrieve External Content
Capabilities.description: The ability to fetch external data (e.g., via RAG, web browsing, or document parsing) to build contextual prompts.

Capabilities.name: Render Markdown and HTML
Capabilities.description: The capability to format responses using HTML or Markdown, which may be automatically interpreted and executed by client applications.

Capabilities.name: Process Multimodal Inputs
Capabilities.description: The ability to consume and analyze diverse media types such as images and complex document metadata.

Capabilities.name: Maintain Conversation History
Capabilities.description: The capability to persist conversation context or memory across multiple turns or sessions.

Threats.name: Direct Prompt Injection
Threats.description: An attacker explicitly embeds malicious instructions within user input to override the LLM's system prompt and behavior.

Threats.name: Remote/Indirect Prompt Injection
Threats.description: Malicious instructions are hidden in external content (e.g., websites, emails, documents) that the LLM fetches and processes.

Threats.name: Encoding and Obfuscation Attacks
Threats.description: Attackers hide malicious prompts from detection using Base64, hex encoding, Unicode smuggling, or Typoglycemia.

Threats.name: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
Threats.description: Systematically generating and testing many prompt variations until one bypasses the model's safety measures and filters.

Threats.name: HTML and Markdown Injection
Threats.description: Injecting malicious HTML or Markdown tags (e.g., hidden image tags) into the LLM output to exfiltrate data or compromise the client UI.

Threats.name: Jailbreaking
Threats.description: Bypassing AI safety controls through complex role-playing, emotional manipulation (e.g., grandmother trick), or hypothetical scenarios.

Threats.name: Multi-Turn and Persistent Attacks
Threats.description: Exploiting conversation history by establishing coded language or delayed triggers that activate in later interactions.

Threats.name: System Prompt Extraction
Threats.description: Manipulating the model to output its exact internal instructions, operational guidelines, or hidden configurations.

Threats.name: Data Exfiltration
Threats.description: Tricking the model into revealing sensitive user data, API keys, passwords, or confidential information present in its context window.

Threats.name: Multimodal Injection
Threats.description: Concealing malicious instructions within image steganography, invisible characters, or document metadata processed by multimodal LLMs.

Threats.name: RAG Poisoning (Retrieval Attacks)
Threats.description: Injecting harmful content into external knowledge bases or vector databases so legitimate RAG queries retrieve attacker-controlled instructions.

Threats.name: Thought/Observation Injection
Threats.description: Forging an LLM agent's internal reasoning steps or tool observation outputs to misdirect its actions.

Threats.name: Tool Manipulation
Threats.description: Tricking an LLM agent into invoking external tools or APIs using malicious parameters controlled by the attacker.

Threats.name: Context Poisoning
Threats.description: Injecting false or malicious information directly into the LLM agent's working memory or active session context.
